questions.question: What are the four core surfaces of a 2026 terminal coding agent harness?
options: Prompt, Response, Retry, Log
Plan, Act, Observe, Recover
Read, Write, Search, Commit
Parse, Execute, Verify, Deploy
questions.explanation: The harness is organized as Plan (maintains a TodoWrite-style state object), Act (dispatches tool calls), Observe (captures and feeds back outputs), and Recover (handles tool errors without blowing the context window).

questions.question: Which transport does MCP use in its 2026 revision for networked tool servers?
options: stdio with JSON-RPC
gRPC bidirectional streaming
StreamableHTTP
WebSocket
questions.explanation: The 2026 MCP revision specifies StreamableHTTP: a long-lived HTTP connection with bidirectional streaming that replaces the earlier SSE and stdio transports.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the PreCompact hook in the cost-control strategy described in this capstone?
options: Block destructive shell commands before they run
Summarize older turns into a prior-state block to free context budget
Emit a final OpenTelemetry trace bundle on session end
Initialize the per-session dollar budget at the start of a run
questions.explanation: The PreCompact hook fires at the 150k-token mark and summarizes older turns into a prior-state block, freeing room for new observations without losing the plan.

questions.question: What does pass@1 measure in the SWE-bench evaluation context?
options: The fraction of tasks solved after unlimited retries
The fraction of tasks solved on the first run without retry or test-set peeking
The fraction of tests that pass on the first compile
The token efficiency ratio compared to a baseline harness
questions.explanation: pass@1 is the fraction of SWE-bench tasks the harness solves on the first run, without peeking at the test set or retrying with test feedback.

questions.question: Why does the harness use git worktrees rather than cloning the repo for each task?
options: Worktrees are faster to create and disposable without touching the main clone
GitHub API requires worktrees for fine-grained permissions
Worktrees enable multi-agent parallel access to the same branch
The CI system cannot detect changes made in a plain clone
questions.explanation: A linked git worktree at a separate path is fast to create and can be torn down on success or failure without affecting the main checkout, making it ideal as a disposable per-task sandbox.

questions.question: At which three layers does the capstone enforce cost control on long agent runs?
options: Per-file read limit, per-tool call limit, per-PR size limit
Per-turn token ceiling, per-session dollar budget, hard turn limit
Per-repo hour limit, per-coder token budget, per-merge dollar cap
Input token cap, output token cap, embedding token cap
questions.explanation: Cost control is enforced at a per-turn token ceiling, a per-session dollar budget, and a hard turn limit (typically 50), preventing runaway spending on difficult tasks.
